summary:
Prometheus: Team Tight Cannons (NASA Space Apps 2026, Flame in Freefall)

Fire behaves differently in space. Without gravity, hot air doesn’t rise, so still air smothers a flame but a gentle ventilation draft can feed it. Earth-based safety tests can therefore be wrong. NASA saw acrylic burn at just 14.8% oxygen in orbit, while silicone that burned on Earth did not burn in space. This matters because Artemis and Mars missions plan oxygen-rich cabins, and crews in orbit cannot evacuate.

Prometheus is an offline fire-safety app for spacecraft cabins. Users set oxygen, pressure, gravity, airflow and material, and instantly see whether a fire would spread, how fast, and the quickest way to stop it. It combines a physics model calibrated to 231 real NASA tests (accuracy improved from 82% to 97%), 400 simulations per scenario to measure uncertainty, and two AI models. One of them is 95% accurate on NASA tests it never saw.

In orbit, ventilation is both the hazard and the cure.
